summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived overview of the Roman Republic, covering its traditional dates (509 BC to 27 BC), its expansion to dominate the Mediterranean, and the wars and political crises that ended it. It discusses the Punic Wars and Carthage's destruction, Pyrrhus and Hannibal in Italy, the Gallic sack of Rome, the First Triumvirate and Caesar's rise, the Catilinarian conspiracy, the civil wars of Marius and Sulla, and the slide toward Augustus's principate. It also touches on Roman literature, the assembly system, daily life, slavery, and the navy.
one_line: Overview of the Roman Republic (509–27 BC), its expansion, Punic and civil wars, Caesar's rise, and its end under Octavian.
key_facts: The Roman Republic is traditionally dated from the overthrow of the Roman Kingdom in 509 BC to the establishment of the Roman Empire in 27 BC.
Most historians use 27 BC, when the Roman Senate granted extraordinary powers to Octavian and he adopted the title Augustus, as the defining end of the Republic.
The Gauls led by chieftain Brennus defeated a Roman army of approximately 15,000 troops at the Battle of Allia River around 390–387 BC and sacked Rome.
Pyrrhus withdrew from Italy after heavy losses, which gave rise to the term "Pyrrhic victory"; he met the Romans again at the Battle of Beneventum in 275 BC.
Hannibal was recalled to Africa and defeated at the Battle of Zama, and Hasdrubal Barca was defeated decisively on the Metaurus River.
Carthage was besieged, stormed and completely destroyed in the Third Punic War, after which Rome acquired all of Carthage's North African and Iberian territories.
The Jugurthine War of 111–104 BC was fought between Rome and Jugurtha of the North African kingdom of Numidia and marked the final Roman pacification of Northern Africa.
The First Triumvirate of Gaius Julius Caesar, Marcus Licinius Crassus and Pompey was formed by 59 BC as an unofficial power-sharing alliance.
Crassus invaded the Parthian Empire in 53 BC and was surrounded, slaughtered and killed at the Battle of Carrhae.
In 51 BC some senators demanded Caesar surrender his armies before standing for consul, and Caesar chose civil war instead.
Caesar crossed the Rubicon in 49 BC and Pompey was decisively defeated at the Battle of Pharsalus in 48 BC, after which Pompey fled to Egypt and was murdered.
Caesar was assassinated by a group of senators at a meeting of the Senate in March 44 BC, and Mark Antony was later defeated at the Battle of Mutina.
Lucius Sergius Catilina led a conspiracy set in motion in 63 BC; consul Marcus Tullius Cicero intercepted his messages and Catiline's forces were cut to pieces by a Roman army.
The Comitia Centuriata, the assembly of the centuries, could declare war and ratify the results of a census, and elected consuls and praetors.
The Roman navy was upgraded in the late Republic, with Caesar assembling an invasion fleet in the English Channel and Pompey clearing Cilician pirates from the Mediterranean.

entities.name: Julius Caesar
entities.role: Roman general and politician who held the dictatorship, gained permanent tribunician powers, and was assassinated in March 44 BC

entities.name: Pompey
entities.role: Roman general and member of the First Triumvirate who was defeated by Caesar at the Battle of Pharsalus and murdered in Egypt

entities.name: Marcus Licinius Crassus
entities.role: member of the First Triumvirate who invaded Parthia and died at the Battle of Carrhae

entities.name: Mark Antony
entities.role: Caesar's lieutenant who condemned Caesar's assassination and was defeated at the Battle of Mutina

entities.name: Octavian
entities.role: Caesar's adopted son and heir who was granted extraordinary powers by the Senate and took the title Augustus in 27 BC

entities.name: Hannibal
entities.role: Carthaginian commander who smashed a succession of Roman consular armies before being recalled to Africa and defeated at Zama

entities.name: Pyrrhus
entities.role: king who invaded Italy, withdrew after costly victories, and met Rome at the Battle of Beneventum in 275 BC

entities.name: Brennus
entities.role: Gallic chieftain who defeated the Roman army at the Battle of Allia River and sacked Rome

entities.name: Lucius Sergius Catilina
entities.role: aristocrat who led a movement based in Faesulae and a conspiracy set in motion in 63 BC

entities.name: Marcus Tullius Cicero
entities.role: consul in 63 BC who intercepted Catiline's messages and had the top conspirators executed

entities.name: Jugurtha
entities.role: king of the North African kingdom of Numidia who fought Rome in the Jugurthine War

entities.name: Scipio Africanus
entities.role: Roman commander who sent an army to Africa to threaten the Carthaginian capital

entities.name: Gaius Marius
entities.role: general whose clash with Lucius Cornelius Sulla started civil wars from 88 BC

entities.name: Lucius Cornelius Sulla
entities.role: general whose army entered Rome at the Battle of the Colline Gate

entities.name: Hasdrubal Barca
entities.role: brother of Hannibal who was defeated decisively on the Metaurus River

entities.name: Virgil
entities.role: author who represents the pinnacle of Roman epic poetry with the Aeneid

entities.name: Lucretius
entities.role: author of On the Nature of Things, which explicated science in an epic poem

entities.name: Battle of Carrhae
entities.role: battle in which Crassus's army was surrounded and slaughtered and Crassus perished

entities.name: Battle of Pharsalus
entities.role: battle in 48 BC where Pompey was decisively defeated by Caesar

entities.name: Battle of Zama
entities.role: battle where Hannibal was defeated

entities.name: Battle of Allia River
entities.role: battle around 390–387 BC where Gauls defeated the Romans

entities.name: Rubicon River
entities.role: legal boundary of Roman Italy that Caesar crossed in 49 BC

entities.name: Palatine Hill
entities.role: elegant hill in Rome whose residences gave the word "palace" its origin

entities.name: Carthage
entities.role: North African city destroyed in the Third Punic War after Rome demanded surrender

entities.name: Numidia
entities.role: North African kingdom whose ruler Jugurtha fought Rome

entities.name: Comitia Centuriata
entities.role: assembly of the centuries that elected consuls and praetors and could declare war

entities.name: First Triumvirate
entities.role: unofficial political alliance formed by 59 BC between Caesar, Crassus and Pompey

entities.name: Roman Senate
entities.role: body that granted extraordinary powers to Octavian and that governed the Republic's laws in its era
